findings.evidence: grep of the file shows the only public declarations are l.121 `g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum`, l.192 the `IsRootSystem` instance, l.198 `span_coroot_...`, l.311 `g2SimplyConnectedBase`, l.335 `g2SimplyConnectedBase_support`, l.360 `hasCartanType_...`; no `root`/`coroot`/pairing lemma among them. `DynkinType.lean:228-239` shows the project's `(rfl)`-without-`@[expose]` idiom for exactly this.
findings.fix: Make `g2Root`/`g2Coroot` public and add public `@[simp]` lemmas characterizing the fields: `g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum.root = g2Root`, `... .coroot = g2Coroot`, and `g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum.toLinearMap x y = x ⬝ᵥ y` (all provable by `(rfl)`, so no body exposure needed).
findings.issue: `g2Root` (l.57), `g2Coroot` (l.64) and `g2Pairing` (l.100) are `private` and `g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum` is not `@[expose]`, and no public lemma restates the fields. Downstream (CFSG L0) the twelve roots, the coroots and the perfect pairing are unavailable — the datum is as opaque as a `Classical.choose`d one, which the PR description says it exists to avoid.

findings.evidence: `DynkinType.lean:400`: `HasCartanType b t := ∃ e : b.support ≃ Fin t.rank, ...`; the file's only other public fact about indices is `g2SimplyConnectedBase_support = {0,1}` (l.335), and `g2SimpleRootIndex`/`g2SimplyConnectedBaseEquiv` are private (l.139, l.343).
findings.fix: Add public lemmas pinning the numbering, e.g. `pairingIn ℤ g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum 0 1 = -1` and `... 1 0 = -3` (equivalently `g2SimplyConnectedBase.cartanMatrix` at the two off-diagonal entries), plus `g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum.toLinearMap (fundamental weight i) (coroot j) = if i = j then 1 else 0` for the simple indices.
findings.issue: `HasCartanType` quantifies the relabelling existentially (`DynkinType.lean:400`), so `hasCartanType_g2SimplyConnectedRootDatum` does not pin which support index is which Bourbaki node. The docstring claims "root indices 0 and 1 are the short and long simple roots" and `⟨ω_i, α_j^∨⟩ = δ_ij`, but nothing public states either, so no consumer can tell node 1 from node 2 in the pinned datum — the numbering the roadmap's Layer 6 exists to fix.

summary: The pinned G2 datum publishes no characteristic API: every carrier definition is `private` and the datum body is unexposed, so no consumer can compute or even prove anything about `root`, `coroot`, or the pairing. The docstring's conventions (fundamental-weight basis, index 0 short / 1 long) are prose only and unrecoverable downstream, defeating the stated purpose of a concrete carrier over `Classical.choose`.
